_comment: The User-Agent each SDK sends: `keenable-<lang>/<sdk version>`, then `<runtime>/<runtime version>` where the SDK can tell, then `<os>/<arch>` where it can tell, separated by single spaces. Nothing else: no host name, user, path, key or locale. `format` cases are the formatting rule on its own: each part is [name, version]; each of the two is cleaned (every run of characters other than ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `+` and `-` becomes one `-`, the result is cut to 64 characters, then leading and trailing `-` are dropped); a part whose cleaned name is empty is left out, and a part whose cleaned version is empty is its name alone. `sdk` gives, per SDK, the product, the runtime name its own test run reports (null: the SDK sends no runtime) and how many parts its default User-Agent has in that run. `override` cases send a search with a caller's User-Agent set on the client (`client`), on the call (`call`), or both, with the header name in any case; the caller's value is sent instead of the SDK's, exactly as given, the call's over the client's.

format.name: a runtime with no version is its name alone
a part with no name is left out
a name that cleans to nothing is left out
slashes, parentheses and semicolons are cleaned
a long value is cut to 64 characters
a cut that ends in a dash drops it
